reader.requirement: At --std 85 the WRITE operand must resolve to a level-01 logical record of an FD in the File Section, optionally qualified (by file-name), so a working-storage item, a subordinate item, an ambiguous unqualified name, a reference-modified record, a file-name, an SD record and the 2002 WRITE FILE form are refused.

edition-consulted.switches: write-rewrite-file-phrase-2002: WRITE FILE file-name-1 refused below 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: WRITE FILE file-name-1 is legal at 2023 and refused at 85; the record-name rule itself is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is RELEASE's record identity at 85; WRITE on an indexed file, qualification by file-name, and subordinate/ambiguous names are not exercised

probes.printed: W1 ST1=00 / W2 ST1=00 / W3 ST1=00 REC=WWWW9999 / W4 ST2=00 / R ST1=00 REC=BBBB2222 / R ST1=00 REC=WWWW9999
probes.expected: REC OF F1, the second record REC-B, REC IN F1 FROM, and REC OF F2 (sequential-access indexed) all written and read back

probes.printed: COBOL1639 'REC' does not uniquely identify a data item
COBOL1757 'WS-REC' is not a logical record of any file description entry
COBOL1757 'K1' is subordinate to 'REC', which is the logical record of 'F1'
COBOL1757 record-name-1 ... shall not be reference-modified
COBOL1639 'F1' is declared as a file-name
COBOL1692 WRITE may not name the sort-merge file 'SF'
COBOL0900 the FILE phrase of a WRITE or REWRITE statement requires COBOL-2002

reader.notes: ResolveWriteRecord runs ResolveRecordName before the sequential/keyed split, so the indexed arm is under the rule; the identity test is FileModel.Records membership.
